title: New York AI data center fight comes to Geneva
content:
New York AI data center fight comes to Geneva, Seneca Lake Monday
New Yorkers are set to gather Monday in Geneva to raise concerns about the potential development of artificial intelligence data-center operations at the Greenidge Generation site on Seneca Lake.
The facility is in the Yates County village of Dresden, in the town of Torrey. Greenidge Generation Holdings changed its corporate name to Vulcan Infrastructure and Power in July. The company operates power-generation and cryptocurrency-mining infrastructure at the site.
The company is pursuing AI and high-performance computing development in Dresden and has discussed 60 megawatts of grid-interconnection capacity to support those plans. The project remains in development.
State Sen. Kristen Gonzalez, D-Queens, is visiting communities across New York as part of her “New York Fights AI Data Centers” tour. The tour includes 13 sites with active or proposed data centers and runs through Aug. 30.
Geneva rally planned Monday
Gonzalez is scheduled to hold a “Seneca Lake Fights AI Data Centers” rally and news conference at noon Monday at the Finger Lakes Welcome Center, 35 Lakefront Drive in Geneva.
The event is being held with Seneca Lake Guardian and the National Coalition Against Cryptomining. Gonzalez is also scheduled to join community members for a 3 p.m. boat ride on Seneca Lake, where participants are expected to view the Dresden facility from the water. The boat ride is invite-only but open to the press.
The tour is scheduled to continue Tuesday in Orangeburg, Wednesday in East Fishkill, Thursday in Albany, Friday in Lansing and Saturday in the Syracuse area.
What Gonzalez wants Hochul to sign
Gonzalez is urging Gov. Kathy Hochul to sign the Responsible Data Center Development Act, which passed both chambers of the state Legislature with bipartisan support in June.
The Assembly version of the measure, A11560, passed the Assembly and Senate on June 4. The Senate substituted the Assembly bill for Gonzalez's companion bill, S10642.
The legislation would establish requirements for public participation and transparency, energy efficiency, labor standards and benefits for communities that host large data centers. It also would require utilities to create separate electricity and water service classifications for qualifying large energy-use facilities.
The bill would impose a one-year moratorium on specified state Department of Environmental Conservation permits for new large data centers with peak demand of at least 20 megawatts. After the moratorium, the measure would require future projects to meet energy-efficiency standards, hold public hearings and undergo environmental-impact analysis.
New York already has a limited data center moratorium
Hochul signed Executive Order 62 on July 14, temporarily pausing certain state environmental permits associated with the construction or expansion of data centers capable of using at least 50 megawatts of electricity.
The moratorium applies to discretionary permits and other approvals issued by the state Department of Environmental Conservation. Projects whose DEC applications were deemed complete before July 14 generally are not covered, and the order does not suspend local government approvals.
The pause is expected to remain in effect while the state develops environmental standards and a regulatory framework for the industry, a process the governor's office said could take up to one year.
The governor's office said the moratorium is intended to protect ratepayers, the environment, the electric grid and communities while the state examines the potential effects of data centers on energy demand, water use, water quality and air quality.
“As data center development threatens to hike up utility bills, deplete our natural resources, and create uncertainty for New Yorkers, it’s my responsibility to take action and lead,” Hochul said when she announced the moratorium.
Vulcan pursuing AI development in Dresden
The Dresden facility has operated as a cryptocurrency-mining operation while also generating electricity.
In May, Greenidge said it had received a proposed interconnection agreement from New York State Electric & Gas for 60 megawatts of non-curtailable power. The company said the agreement, if completed, would advance its plans for AI and high-performance computing development at the Dresden site.
More recent company materials describe the site as having 64 megawatts of existing behind-the-meter data-center capacity that could transition from bitcoin mining to AI and high-performance computing, along with 60 megawatts of grid-interconnection capacity.
The company said its transition to Vulcan Infrastructure and Power reflects a broader strategy focused on power generation and digital infrastructure, including sites capable of supporting AI and high-performance computing workloads.
Opponents have raised concerns about the potential effects of additional data-center operations on Seneca Lake, noise, emissions, electricity use and surrounding communities. Those concerns are expected to be discussed during Monday's rally.
Proposed data centers could require nearly 12,000 megawatts
Gonzalez's office says 38 large data-center projects are proposed in the New York Independent System Operator's interconnection queue.
If all those projects were developed, they would require more than 11,900 megawatts of additional electricity demand, according to the senator's office. Hochul's executive order separately states that, as of May 2026, nearly 12,000 megawatts of data-center load requests were in the NYISO queue.
Gonzalez and environmental advocates say the growth could increase utility costs, strain the electric grid and increase demand for water and other resources.
The data-center industry has become a major economic-development and environmental issue as demand grows for computing power, particularly for artificial intelligence.

report.summary: 纽约州AI数据中心之争蔓延至日内瓦，反对者集会抗议塞内卡湖新建项目。
report.background: 随着AI算力需求激增，数据中心建设在全美引发环境与能源争议。纽约州塞内卡湖的格林尼治发电站原为加密货币矿场，现更名为Vulcan Infrastructure and Power，计划转型AI高性能计算，并向电网申请60兆瓦容量。反对者担忧其加剧噪音、排放和用电负担。州参议员冈萨雷斯发起“纽约对抗AI数据中心”巡回活动，在日内瓦举行抗议，并敦促州长签署《负责任数据中心发展法案》。此前州长已签署第62号行政令，暂停部分大型数据中心的环境许可。
key_points: 格林尼治站点转型：原比特币矿场Vulcan计划在德累斯顿发展AI算力，现有64兆瓦自备容量及60兆瓦并网申请。
反对集会：周一在日内瓦举行“塞内卡湖对抗AI数据中心”集会，联合环保组织抗议，下午乘船视察现场。
立法推动：冈萨雷斯呼吁州长签署《负责任数据中心发展法案》，设一年暂停期并要求能效、公听和环评。
州长行政令：7月已暂缓50兆瓦以上数据中心的DEC许可，最长一年，以制定监管框架。
规模惊人：纽约ISO队列中有38个大型项目，若全部建成需新增约1.2万兆瓦电力需求。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，纽约的监管趋严可能推高数据中心建设成本，促使企业选择其他州或优化能效。对开发者来说，算力供给和电价可能受影响，间接影响云服务价格。对普通用户，数据中心可能推高电费、消耗水资源，但也会带来就业和税收，社区需在发展与环保间权衡。若法案通过，全美或效仿类似审查机制，重塑AI基础设施格局。
report.tools: 可关注NYISO电网互联队列以跟踪项目进展，阅读DEC行政令文本，使用EPAs ENERGY STAR数据中心能效工具评估PUE。开源项目如OpenAI的Datacentre PUE监测或Linux基金会绿色软件基金会的Impact Framework可辅助测算碳足迹。
